q: ∫₀² f(x) dx is an area, so it can never be negative.
why: Myth. It's a signed area: parts below the x-axis count as negative. ∫₀² (−1) dx = −2.

q: Why do you add + C to an indefinite integral?
o: Every constant has derivative 0, so many functions share the same derivative
It's only there to look neat
why: x² + 1, x² − 7 and x² all have derivative 2x. + C covers all of them.
The antiderivative is x². From 1 to 3: 9 − 1 = 8.

q: ∫₀¹ f·g dx = (∫₀¹ f dx) · (∫₀¹ g dx)
why: Almost always false. With f = g = x: ∫₀¹ x² dx = 1/3, but (1/2)·(1/2) = 1/4. It works by luck for constants.
